transcript.content: Hi, it's good to meet you. What brings you in today?

Hi. Nice to meet you too. 

I came in today because... well, I just can't stop worrying about everything at once. It's just constant. I'm constantly worrying about my marriage, whether my performance is slipping at work, paying the bills... even the house projects I keep starting and then dropping. I just get stuck worrying about whether I'm basically failing as a husband and a father. It's just taking over everything.
When you start worrying, is it hard for you to stop or control it?

Yeah, it's really hard to stop. I try to control it, but... even when I tell myself to just focus on the code in front of me at work, or try to breathe through a workout, it doesn't work. 

One concern just hooks another. Before I know it, I'm twenty steps ahead, imagining a bad review turning into losing my job, and then my family being worse off because of me. I just can't shut it down once it starts.
How long have you been feeling this constant, hard-to-control worry?

It's been going on for about nine months now. I think it really started when the cloud migration project at work ramped up, and right around the same time, the arguments at home started becoming a regular thing. Since then, it's just been constant.
Do you feel your worry is mainly tied to the problems at work and home that started nine months ago?

Well, I mean... those things definitely kicked it off, but no, it's not just tied to that anymore. 

Like I said, I worry about everything now. Even if work is going okay for a day, or things are quiet at home, my brain just finds something else. I'll worry about the bills, or those house projects, or just... whether I'm doing enough in general. It's like the worry just spread to every part of my life, even the stuff that isn't actually a problem right now.
Do you find yourself doing any repetitive rituals or mental routines to try to reduce the worry?

No, not really. I don't have any... rituals or anything like that. I mean, I don't count things or have a specific routine I have to do to make the anxiety stop, if that's what you mean. 

I mostly just sit there and let the thoughts run, or I try to force myself to look at my screen and keep coding. But there's no repetitive action or mental checklist I'm doing to try and cancel the worry out. It just stays stuck in my head.
Over the past couple of weeks, have you been feeling down or depressed most of the day?

No, I wouldn't say I've been feeling depressed. I mean, I'm definitely exhausted from all the worrying, and that can drag me down, but I don't feel sad or... hopeless, if that makes sense. It's just the constant anxiety that's the issue, not feeling down.
Have you been feeling restless or on edge a lot?

Yeah, definitely. I feel wound tight almost all day. It's like... my shoulders are just locked up, and I'm constantly bracing for something bad to happen. 

And sitting still is really hard. I catch myself pacing around the house between work meetings. Even when I try to do something I enjoy, like going to chess club, I can't just sit there. I end up tapping the pieces or fidgeting the whole time because sitting still just feels impossible right now.
Do you find that you get tired easily?

No, I wouldn't say so. I know I mentioned earlier that I feel exhausted, but that's more of a mental drain by the end of the day from being so tense. As far as just getting tired easily physically during the day... no, I haven't really noticed that. If anything, I'm usually too wired to feel sleepy.
Have you been having trouble concentrating?

Yeah, definitely. It's actually been a real problem at work lately. During sprint planning or when I'm doing code reviews, I'll catch myself reading the same design note three or four times. And I still end up missing details because... well, part of my mind is just off somewhere else. I'll be sitting there, but in my head, I'm calculating what I might have forgotten at home, or worrying about how badly the next argument with someone is going to go. It's like I just can't keep my focus on what's right in front of me.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yeah, sleep has been really rough. Most nights, I'll get into bed and I'm just physically exhausted, but my brain... it just won't shut off. I just lie there running through all the risks on my current project at work, or worrying about money, or agonizing over something I said to my wife earlier. 

And then, even when I finally do manage to drift off, I almost always wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning. Once I'm up, that's it. I can't get back to sleep because I'm already lying there rehearsing all the problems I have to deal with the next day. It's just a constant cycle.
Have you been feeling more irritable than usual?

No, not really. I know I mentioned agonizing over an argument with my wife earlier, but that's... well, it's not really because I'm snapping at her or feeling angry. It's more about me just being overwhelmed with worry. As far as feeling irritable or short-tempered in general, no, I haven't really noticed that. I'm mostly just anxious.
Over the past two weeks, have you lost interest or pleasure in things you usually enjoy?

No, I don't think so. I still enjoy the things I usually like doing. I mean, sometimes it's a little hard to fully relax and just get into a game or a project because my mind is still racing with all the stuff I'm worried about, but... the actual interest is definitely still there. I haven't lost the desire to do my hobbies or anything like that.
If the problems at work and at home were to settle down, do you think this anxiety would mostly go away?

I... I don't really think so. I'd like to say yes, but honestly, probably not. 

It seems like even when things are actually going fine at work, and there aren't any immediate issues at home, my mind just finds something else to latch onto. It's like my brain just always needs a problem to fixate on. If it's not a software deployment, it'll be, you know, worrying about the car breaking down, or a bill, or just something completely random. 

So... no, I don't think it would just disappear. I'd probably just shift to worrying about whatever is next on the list.
